name: Question 14
problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal.
worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}},$ $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}},$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{3}}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{2\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot 3+(-5)\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot 1}{(-1)^{2}+{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=(-1)[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{2\cdot 3+(-2)\cdot 1+(-5)\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot 0}{{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{2\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 0+(-5)\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{3}=(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $x$ coincides with the projection, the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ is zero $0.$

Consider the vector x and the subspace S=Span{a1,a2,a3} where a1=[−1301],a2=[31−30],a3=[1011],x=[2−2−5−3]. Find the distance between x and the subspace S given that the set {a1,a2,a3} is orthogonal.

EXPLANATION

Since the set {a1,a2,a3} is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of x onto the subspace S is given by

projSx=proja1x+proja2x+proja3x.

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of x onto Span{a1}, Span{a2}, and Span{a3}:

proja1x=x⋅a1a1⋅a1a1=2⋅(−1)+(−2)⋅3+(−5)⋅0+(−3)⋅1(−1)2+32+02+12a1=(−1)[−1301]=[1−30−1]proja2x=x⋅a2a2⋅a2a2=2⋅3+(−2)⋅1+(−5)⋅(−3)+(−3)⋅032+12+(−3)2+02a2=[31−30]proja3x=x⋅a3a3⋅a3a3=2⋅1+(−2)⋅0+(−5)⋅1+(−3)⋅112+02+12+12a3=(−2)[1011]=[−20−2−2]

Therefore, we have that projSx=proja1x+proja2x+proja3x=[1−30−1]+[31−30]+[−20−2−2]=[2−2−5−3]=x.

Since x coincides with the projection, the distance between x and the subspace S is zero 0.
